app.name: Rooted
app.tagline: Money skills that start from where you live.
app.disclaimer: Education, not financial advice. Figures are simplified and checked against the sources shown.

scam.keys: Tip: press S for scam, L for legitimate.

learn.title: Your lessons in {countryIn}
learn.intro: Short lessons written for your country, language and stage of life, using only checked facts.
learn.compareTitle: The same lesson in different countries
learn.error: This lesson could not be loaded. Try again, or read a saved version.
learn.aiLabel: Written by AI from the checked facts below. Reviewed facts, not reviewed wording.

first-paycheck.title: First pay day
first-paycheck.body: Your first salary of {income} lands in your account. How much do you put aside each month?

frugal.label: Save 25%
frugal.hint: Grows fast, but life feels tight.

family-budget.title: The family budget
family-budget.body: With a household of {income} a month, bills and children compete for every unit. How much do you put aside?

retirement-budget.title: Living on a pension
retirement-budget.body: Your pension pays {income} a month and you have savings put by. How much of your savings do you spend?

travel.label: Travel and enjoy it
travel.hint: Draw a lot from savings each month.

where-to-save.title: Where does the money live?
where-to-save.body: Your savings need a home. In {countryIn}, people choose between these.

cash.label: {cashName}
cash.hint: Earns {cashRate}. Can be lost or stolen.

everyday.label: {everydayName}
everyday.hint: Earns {everydayRate}. Easy to spend by accident.

informal.label: Join a {informalName}
informal.hint: Earns {informalRate}. Built on trust in the group.

phone-offer.title: The new phone
phone-offer.body: Your phone breaks. A shop offers the latest model now, on credit at {creditApr} a year.

car.title: Getting around
car.body: Commuting is getting hard. A dealer offers a new car on a loan at {loanApr} a year.

pension.title: Thinking about later
pension.body: In {countryIn}, the system is: {retirementSystem}. Do you add your own savings to a {retirementName}?

insurance.title: Insurance
insurance.body: An insurer offers cover for illness and accidents for about 1% of your income.

skip.label: Skip it
skip.hint: Keep the money, carry the risk.

scam.title: Your phone keeps buzzing
scam.body: Fraudsters target people in {countryIn} with very local tricks. Can you tell which messages are real?

emergency.title: Something goes wrong
emergency.body: A medical bill and a repair arrive in the same month. You have {cash} in savings. How do you pay?

savings.label: Use savings first
savings.hint: Anything missing goes on a card at {creditApr}.

family.label: Ask family
family.hint: No interest, but it costs goodwill.

sell-investments.label: Sell investments
sell-investments.hint: Selling in a hurry often means selling low.

invest.title: A little extra
invest.body: Your savings are growing. A colleague says a new coin will triple. A bank offers a {indexName}.

index.label: Invest monthly in the {indexName}
index.hint: Ups and downs, historically about {indexRate} a year.

child-education.title: Your child's education
child-education.body: Your child is starting high school. How do you pay for it?

education-loan.label: Take an education loan
education-loan.hint: Pay over years, at {loanApr} a year.

family-support.title: Family asks for help
family-support.body: {familySupport}. They ask if you can help.

decline.label: Say no this time
decline.hint: Your savings stay, the relationship strains.

parents-care.title: Your parents need care
parents-care.body: Your parents are getting older and their costs are rising. How do you support them?

quick-job.label: Take the first job offered
quick-job.hint: Back to work fast, slightly lower pay.

nest-egg.title: Your nest egg
nest-egg.body: Part of your savings is invested. A friendly adviser offers a scheme that is "guaranteed 12% a year".

all-cash.label: Move everything to cash
all-cash.hint: No ups and downs, loses to inflation.

family-request.title: A family milestone
family-request.body: A grandchild's {grandchildMilestone} is coming up and the family hopes you will help.

housing.title: A home that is too big
housing.body: The children have moved out. Your home costs a lot to heat and keep up.

late-work.title: Still able to work
late-work.body: A local business would love your experience part-time.

estate.title: Putting things in order
estate.body: Friends talk about wills and who decides if they fall ill.

make-will.label: Write a will and set a power of attorney
make-will.hint: A small fee, peace of mind.

skip.label: Leave it for now
skip.hint: Free, but family may argue later.

home.title: Three lives, three countries.
home.intro: Each person plays the same Life Path, but by their own country's rules: its banks, prices, safety nets and scams.
home.custom: Or set up your own profile

maya.name: Maya
maya.about: 24, first full-time job in logistics. Has a credit card balance and a new 401(k) at work.

ananya.name: Ananya
ananya.about: 42, works in IT, two children in school. Pays for almost everything with UPI.

brigitte.name: Brigitte
brigitte.about: 68, retired teacher living on her pension and savings. Plays in German.

hub.title: Your money line in {countryIn}
hub.intro: Six stations: understand how money works where you live, learn two topics, try them on your own numbers, then put it all together in the Life Path game.
hub.guideAbout: Banks, interest, inflation, borrowing, safety nets and local scams, with sources.
hub.lessonAbout: A short lesson written for your country and stage of life, then three quick questions.
hub.gameAbout: Live through the next decades of decisions and see where your money goes.

guide.intro: The basics of your country's money system in one page. Every figure is a checked fact with its source.
guide.inflation: Prices rise by about {rate} a year (inflation).
guide.worldBankInflation: World Bank figure for {year}: {rate}. Official statistics take time to publish, so this is older than the figure above.
guide.accountOwnership: {share} of adults here have a bank or mobile-money account (World Bank Global Findex, {year}).
guide.policyRate: The central bank ({bank}) key interest rate is about {rate}. Savings and loan rates follow it.
guide.pricesWhy: If your money earns less than inflation, it buys a little less every year.
guide.creditBureau: Your credit record is kept by: {bureau}.
guide.regulator: Banks and payment providers are supervised by {regulator}.
guide.scamsTitle: Scams people here fall for, and real messages

tools.title: Tools
tools.intro: Try the ideas from the lessons on your own numbers, with your country's real rates.

budget.title: Budget planner
budget.about: Split your monthly income with the 50/30/20 rule and see how fast you can build a cushion.
budget.cushionBody: A common goal is 3 to 6 months of needs: {low} to {high}.
budget.afterYear: Saved for a year in a {name} at {rate}

growth.title: Savings growth
growth.about: See what saving a fixed amount every month becomes in cash, in savings, and in an index fund.
growth.today: Worth {value} in today's money (prices rising {rate} a year)
growth.chart: How it grows, year by year
growth.note: Savings and fund rates are this country's figures. Index funds go up and down; the line uses their long-term average, not a promise.

debt.title: Debt payoff
debt.about: See how long a balance takes to clear, and what the interest really costs.
debt.never: Never paid off: the payment doesn't cover the interest.
debt.note: Paying more each month cuts both the time and the interest. At very high rates, a small payment can mean the debt never goes away.

story.drawdown: Taken from savings to live on
story.lostDetail: Cash at home or in an informal group can disappear.
story.sourceNote: Every figure is calculated from the real rates in {countryIn} shown in the country guide; the market's yearly ups and downs are drawn at random but stay the same if you replay.

market.title: Choose where your extra savings go
market.intro: Four options are on the table. Look at the news and the numbers, then pick one.

index.news: Markets ended the year mixed; long-term savers kept buying every month.

savings.news: Rates follow the central bank, now at {rate}.

stock.name: NovaGrid Energy
stock.news: "Next big thing": shares soar after record orders, but the company still loses money.

coin.name: ZapCoin
coin.kind: Crypto token · tip from a colleague
coin.news: Social media influencer: "100x by summer!" No company, product or profits behind it.

market.youPickedBest: Good pick: the index fund is usually the best home for long-term money.
market.bestIs: The best long-term pick here is the {name}.
market.whyIndex: It spreads your money over hundreds of companies, costs little, and has years to recover from bad patches. Money you need soon still belongs in savings.

why.keep-saving: Savings are safe, but over many years they barely keep up with prices.
why.single-stock: One company can fall by half in a bad year. Big recent gains say little about the future.
why.crypto-tip: With no business behind it, its price depends only on hype. Tips from social media are how many people lose money.

market.note: Practice market. The fund and savings figures are real figures from {countryIn}; NovaGrid and ZapCoin are made up to show common traps.
